authors: Erkki Oja
title: A simplified neuron model as a principal component analyzer
annotation: Foundational stabilized Hebbian rule; principal-component learning under specified assumptions. Start here for the mathematical distinction between correlation and useful normalized learning.

authors: Elie L. Bienenstock; Leon N. Cooper; Paul W. Munro
title: Theory for the development of neuron selectivity: orientation specificity and binocular interaction in visual cortex
annotation: Sliding modification threshold links activity history to plasticity and selectivity. Biological foundation, not an LLM experiment.

authors: Terence D. Sanger
title: Optimal unsupervised learning in a single-layer linear feedforward neural network
annotation: Generalized Hebbian learning extracts multiple eigenvectors. Important for understanding decorrelation and the limits of linear representation objectives.

authors: John J. Hopfield
title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities
annotation: Classical recurrent associative memory and retrieval from incomplete cues. Distinguish pattern storage and retrieval from training a deep representation system.

authors: Guo-qiang Bi; Mu-ming Poo
title: Synaptic modifications in cultured hippocampal neurons: dependence on spike timing, synaptic strength, and postsynaptic cell type
annotation: Experimental STDP foundation. Supports timing-sensitive plasticity in the studied neurons, not a universal rule for every brain synapse.

authors: Eugene M. Izhikevich
title: Solving the distal reward problem through linkage of STDP and dopamine signaling
annotation: Computational eligibility-trace and neuromodulation mechanism for delayed reward. A useful precursor to three-factor learning.

authors: James L. McClelland; Bruce L. McNaughton; Randall C. O'Reilly
title: Why there are complementary learning systems in the hippocampus and neocortex: insights from the successes and failures of connectionist models of learning and memory
annotation: Fast acquisition, slow integration, and interleaving motivate memory consolidation. Does not imply that all fast/slow ML architectures are faithful biological models.

authors: Jürgen Schmidhuber
title: Learning to control fast-weight memories: An alternative to dynamic recurrent networks
annotation: Slow controller produces fast memory changes. Historical source for learned fast-weight programming; related technical-report work appeared in 1991.

authors: Jimmy Ba; Geoffrey E. Hinton; Volodymyr Mnih; Joel Z. Leibo; Catalin Ionescu
title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
annotation: Fast connections store recent activity and support attention-like retrieval. A bridge from biological timescales to sequence-model engineering.

authors: Dmitry Krotov; John J. Hopfield
title: Unsupervised learning by competing hidden units
annotation: Competition and local plasticity produce useful hidden features. Separate unsupervised feature learning from supervised readout evaluation.

authors: Leopold Grinberg; John Hopfield; Dmitry Krotov
title: Local Unsupervised Learning for Image Analysis
annotation: Convolutional local learning, patch normalization, and transfer experiments. Relevant to visual representations, not direct LLM evidence.

authors: Timoleon Moraitis; Dmitry Toichkin; Adrien Journé; Yansong Chua; Qinghai Guo
title: SoftHebb: Bayesian Inference in Unsupervised Hebbian Soft Winner-Take-All Networks
annotation: Probabilistic interpretation of soft competitive learning. Its unsupervised objective should not be confused with access to downstream class labels.

authors: Adrien Journé; Hector Garcia Rodriguez; Qinghai Guo; Timoleon Moraitis
title: Hebbian Deep Learning Without Feedback
annotation: Multilayer SoftHebb with image benchmarks and a supervised linear classifier. Key reference for the capability and scaling limits of local feature learning.

authors: Thomas Miconi; Kenneth O. Stanley; Jeff Clune
title: Differentiable plasticity: training plastic neural networks with backpropagation
annotation: Learns effective Hebbian plasticity through an outer gradient loop. Demonstrates rapid memory and meta-learning, rather than elimination of backpropagation.

authors: Thomas Miconi; Aditya Rawal; Jeff Clune; Kenneth O. Stanley
title: Backpropamine: training self-modifying neural networks with differentiable neuromodulated plasticity
annotation: Learned neuromodulation controls plasticity; includes recurrent language-model experiments. Official code: https://github.com/uber-research/backpropamine.

authors: Jack Rae; Chris Dyer; Peter Dayan; Timothy Lillicrap
title: Fast Parametric Learning with Activation Memorization
annotation: Hebbian Softmax supports rapid binding of rare classes. The best reported language result combines multiple memory mechanisms; inspect the ablation table.

authors: Zhongxia Yan; Hanrui Wang; Demi Guo; Song Han
title: MicroNet for Efficient Language Modeling
annotation: A compression system that includes Hebbian Softmax, cache, distillation, pruning, and quantization. Aggregate efficiency gains are not a Hebbian-only effect.

authors: Timothy P. Lillicrap; Daniel Cownden; Douglas B. Tweed; Colin J. Akerman
title: Random synaptic feedback weights support error backpropagation for deep learning
annotation: Feedback alignment relaxes exact weight-transport requirements. Error information still reaches hidden layers.

authors: James C. R. Whittington; Rafal Bogacz
title: An Approximation of the Error Backpropagation Algorithm in a Predictive Coding Network with Local Hebbian Synaptic Plasticity
annotation: Connects local predictive-coding updates with backpropagation under model assumptions. Read for credit assignment and iterative-inference requirements.

authors: Benjamin Scellier; Yoshua Bengio
title: Equilibrium Propagation: Bridging the Gap between Energy-Based Models and Backpropagation
annotation: Gradient learning from free and nudged equilibria. Local correlation differences do not remove the need for a task-dependent teaching influence.

authors: Jordan Guerguiev; Timothy P. Lillicrap; Blake A. Richards
title: Towards deep learning with segregated dendrites
annotation: Compartmentalized neurons separate feedforward and feedback influences. A biologically motivated route to deep credit assignment.

authors: Guillaume Bellec and colleagues
title: A solution to the learning dilemma for recurrent networks of spiking neurons
annotation: E-prop combines local eligibility traces with learning signals. Distinguish exact theoretical decompositions from practical signal approximations.

authors: Sergey Bartunov; Adam Santoro; Blake A. Richards; Luke Marris; Geoffrey E. Hinton; Timothy Lillicrap
title: Assessing the Scalability of Biologically-Motivated Deep Learning Algorithms and Architectures
annotation: Controlled evidence of scaling difficulties for the alternatives tested. Historical comparison, not a verdict on every later method.

authors: Geoffrey Hinton
title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm: Some Preliminary Investigations
annotation: Positive and negative forward passes optimize layer-specific goodness. Small initial demonstrations; not plain pairwise Hebbian learning.

authors: Dmitry Krotov; John J. Hopfield
title: Dense Associative Memory for Pattern Recognition
annotation: Higher-capacity associative models connect to feature and prototype recognition. Foundational context for modern memory networks.

authors: Hubert Ramsauer and colleagues
title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
annotation: Continuous Hopfield retrieval connects to attention. Capacity results have model and pattern assumptions; retrieval equivalence is not training equivalence.

authors: Dmitry Krotov; John Hopfield
title: Large Associative Memory Problem in Neurobiology and Machine Learning
annotation: Relates large associative memories to hidden-neuron models with pairwise interactions. Useful for assessing biological interpretations of modern Hopfield models.

authors: Angelos Katharopoulos; Apoorv Vyas; Nikolaos Pappas; François Fleuret
title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention
annotation: Kernelized linear attention has recurrent accumulators. Normalization requires additional state beyond a bare key-value matrix.

authors: Imanol Schlag; Kazuki Irie; Jürgen Schmidhuber
title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
annotation: Core connection between linear attention and fast weights; replaces additive memory writing with error-correcting delta updates.

authors: Songlin Yang; Bailin Wang; Yu Zhang; Yikang Shen; Yoon Kim
title: Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length
annotation: Parallel training algorithms make delta-rule sequence models practical on modern accelerators. Systems work is central to the scaling story.

authors: Songlin Yang; Jan Kautz; Ali Hatamizadeh
title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
annotation: Combines forgetting gates with error-correcting memory updates. Direct predecessor of delta-based attention in larger hybrid architectures.

authors: Yu Sun and colleagues
title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
publication_status: arXiv paper, July 2024; revised limitations August 31, 2025
annotation: TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP turn recurrent state into an inner learner. Reports experiments from 125M to 1.3B parameters.

authors: Ali Behrouz; Peilin Zhong; Vahab Mirrokni
title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
annotation: Adaptive neural memory uses gradient-based surprise, momentum, and forgetting. Very-long-context retrieval claims are task-specific.

authors: Ali Behrouz; Meisam Razaviyayn; Peilin Zhong; Vahab Mirrokni
title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization, Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization
annotation: MIRAS organizes memory architectures by objective, retention, and learning rule. Useful design framework rather than proof of universal continual learning.

authors: Ali Behrouz; Meisam Razaviyayn; Peilin Zhong; Vahab Mirrokni
title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures
annotation: Multiple optimization timescales and the Hope architecture. Distinguish the conceptual framework from specific demonstrated retention results.

authors: Arnuv Tandon and colleagues
title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
annotation: TTT-E2E adapts a sliding-window transformer with next-token training on context. Reports 3B/164B-token experiments and context-scaling comparisons.

authors: Bo Peng and colleagues
title: RWKV-7 "Goose" with Expressive Dynamic State Evolution
annotation: Richer recurrent state evolution with released language-model evidence around 3B scale. Related through fast state updates, not pure Hebbian pretraining.

authors: Julien Siems; Timur Carstensen; Arber Zela; Frank Hutter; Massimiliano Pontil; Riccardo Grazzi
title: DeltaProduct: Improving State-Tracking in Linear RNNs via Householder Products
publication_status: arXiv paper; revised title verified October 2025 version
annotation: Multiple online update steps produce richer state transitions. Earlier versions used a different subtitle; useful for expressivity versus efficiency.

authors: Kimi Team
title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
annotation: 48B-total/3B-active hybrid KDA–MLA model with matched-recipe comparisons. Speed and KV-cache maxima depend on benchmark context and implementation.

authors: Qwen Team
title: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking
annotation: Documents an 80B-total/3B-active model using a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/attention layout. Architectural adoption evidence, not an isolated Hebbian ablation.

authors: Qwen Team
title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
publication_status: Official model documentation; release announcement August 26, 2026
annotation: Continues Gated DeltaNet with sparse attention and conventional gradient optimizers. Included for current architectural adoption, not leaderboard comparison.

authors: Rui-Jie Zhu; Qihang Zhao; Guoqi Li; Jason K. Eshraghian
title: SpikeGPT: Generative Pre-trained Language Model with Spiking Neural Networks
annotation: 45M and 216M spiking language models trained with backpropagation. Separates spiking representations from Hebbian learning and measured energy efficiency.

authors: Shikuang Deng; Jiayuan Zhang; Yuhang Wu; Ting Chen; Shi Gu
title: Rethinking Hebbian Principle: Low-Dimensional Structural Projection for Unsupervised Learning
annotation: SPHeRe uses structural preservation, orthogonality, and local auxiliary optimization. Includes local backpropagation rather than eliminating gradients everywhere.

authors: Wenjia Hua; Kejie Zhao; Luziwei Leng; Ran Cheng; Yuxin Ma; Qinghai Guo
title: Hebbian Learning with Global Direction
annotation: Oja-style magnitudes are modulated by global gradient signs. The paper explicitly uses a backpropagated gradient, an essential qualification for its scaling claims.

authors: Alexander Demidovskij; Igor Salnikov; Olga Frolova; Aleksei Trutnev; Artyom Tugaryov; Yuri Ignatiev; Vasilisa Blyudova; Egor Zharikov; Irina Novikova
title: Going beyond LoRA Fine-Tuning with Hebb Learning: Blazingly Fast and Accurate
publication_status: ECAI 2025 proceedings; publisher online date August 25, 2026
annotation: LoRA-HeRO combines local updates, layer selection, and gradient fine-tuning. Text-only LLaMA results show a quality tradeoff; inspect the freeze-only ablation.

authors: Xing Zhao; Liu Yang; Xi-Le Zhao; Yueqi Yang; Tianqi Jiang
title: Hebbian-Guided Bi-Directional Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
annotation: HeBiRA reallocates low-rank capacity using activations and output gradients. Direct PEFT evidence, including LLaMA math and code tasks; retains gradient training.

authors: Jinchang Zhu; Jindong Li; Cheng Zhang; Jiahong Liu; Menglin Yang
title: HeLa-Mem: Hebbian Learning and Associative Memory for LLM Agents
publication_status: ACL 2026 long paper, July; preprint April 18
annotation: External episodic graph, semantic consolidation, and spreading-activation retrieval. Strong relevance to agent memory; does not train the underlying LLM synapses.

authors: Riccardo Casciotti; Francesco De Santis; Alberto Antonietti; Annamaria Mesaros
title: Incremental learning for audio classification with Hebbian Deep Neural Networks
publication_status: ICASSP 2026, per paper record; arXiv April 20
annotation: Selective kernel plasticity improves incremental ESC-50 classification in the reported setup. Domain-specific continual-learning evidence.

authors: Andreas Knoblauch
title: Supervised Hebbian learning in Deep Counterstream Associative Networks
annotation: Opposing activity waves support local supervised association. Evidence is binarized MNIST; no demonstrated LLM-scale application.

authors: Luca Pinchetti; Simon Frieder; Thomas Lukasiewicz; Tommaso Salvatori
title: Faster Predictive Coding Networks via Better Initialization
annotation: Addresses iterative inference cost by improving state initialization. Relevant to scalability of local credit assignment, not direct Hebbian LLM evidence.

authors: Daniel Szelogowski
title: Hebbian Memory-Augmented Recurrent Networks: Engram Neurons in Deep Learning
annotation: Explicit differentiable Hebbian traces; includes WikiText-103 with broadly comparable recurrent-baseline performance. Exploratory interpretability and memory contribution.

authors: P. Myles Eugenio
title: Hebbian learning the local structure of language
annotation: Exploratory tokenization and morphology model. Its language-structure claims do not establish competitive open-ended language modeling.

authors: Gavriel Di Nepi; Federico Siciliano; Fabrizio Silvestri
title: Titans Revisited: A Lightweight Reimplementation and Critical Analysis of a Test-Time Memory Model
annotation: Independent reimplementation with mixed outcomes across different tasks. Useful replication evidence, with settings distinct from original autoregressive LM experiments.

authors: Longwei Zou; Lin Zhong
title: KVBuffer: IO-aware Serving for Linear Attention
annotation: Serving study on Qwen3-Next shows the importance of recurrent-state memory traffic. Constant state with context length does not guarantee low latency.
